(Search snippet content — full article 403'd on direct fetch; Al Jazeera's own reporting language)
Sudan has lodged a complaint against Ethiopia with both the United Nations Security Council and the African Union's Peace and Security Council after a series of deadly drone attacks this year. Sudan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused the RSF of using Ethiopian territory to launch "brazen aggression" against "civilian sites and power stations" in Sudan. According to Sudan's army, there were 70 assaults from February 15 to October 27 involving 187 one-way attack drones, which killed or wounded 484 civilians and killed 176 Sudanese soldiers, with another 200 soldiers wounded. Launch sites identified at Asosa Airport in western Ethiopia, the Kurmuk-Gizen border area and Bahir Dar airbase in Amhara.
